title: Procedures for Performing a Failure Mode, Effects and Criticality Analysis
publisher: U.S. Department of Defense (DoD)

licensing_access_notes: Public domain (U.S. Federal Government publication). Standard was cancelled for new DoD designs in August 1998, but remains the universal global benchmark for aerospace FMECA format and logic.

title: NASA Reliability and Maintainability (R&M) Standard for Spaceflight and Support Systems

title: System Design and Analysis
publisher: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA)
relevance_to_fmea_gpt: Classic landmark regulatory guidance for civil transport category aircraft airworthiness compliance with 14 CFR 25.1309. Defines failure severity classes (Catastrophic, Critical/Severe-Major, Major, Minor) and ties them mathematically to inverse probability requirements (< 1e-9, 1e-7, 1e-5), providing qualitative and quantitative FMEA guidelines.
licensing_access_notes: Public domain (U.S. Federal Government publication).
evidence_category_note: FAA Advisory Circulars describe an acceptable (not the only) means of compliance; they are guidance, not regulations.

licensing_access_notes: Public domain (U.S. Federal Government publication).
evidence_category_note: FAA Advisory Circulars describe an acceptable (not the only) means of compliance; they are guidance, not regulations.

title: Determination of Turbine Blade Life From Engine Field Data
publisher: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA Glenn Research Center) & United Airlines

dataset_population_audit.component_scope: CFM56 High-Pressure Turbine Stage 1 (T-1) Rotor Blades
observed_failure_mechanisms: Trailing edge and tip cap distress
dataset_population_audit.statistical_methodology: Johnson-Weibull two-parameter distribution (median rank plotting for multiple censored life data)
dataset_population_audit.generalization_constraint: Empirical removal history specific to audited United Airlines CFM56 T-1 fleet; does NOT represent fleet-wide failure rates across all operators, engine variants, or part number P/N 301-789-204-0.

relevance_to_fmea_gpt: Provides authoritative field data and Johnson-Weibull life analysis on 16 HPT Stage 1 blade sets (1,312 blades total, 111 failed blades) from commercial airline CFM56 engines. Categorizes blade distress into TMF, oxidation/erosion, and mechanical damage, providing empirical Weibull slope parameters (beta ~ 5.235) and failure distributions.
licensing_access_notes: Public domain (U.S. Federal Government publication), hosted on NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS).
technical_domain: HPT stage 1 blade life (field removal data, Weibull)

title: Fretting Stresses in Single Crystal Superalloy Turbine Blade Attachments
authors: Gregory Swanson (NASA Marshall Space Flight Center)
publisher: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center (NTRS) / ASME-STLE International Joint Tribology Conference preprint
document_type: Conference Preprint (NASA MSFC, STI type PREPRINT)
technical_domain: Blade attachment fretting / contact mechanics (3D finite element)

dataset_population_audit.test_article: Single-crystal (PWA 1480/1493) turbine blades of the SSME alternate Advanced High Pressure Fuel Turbopump (HPFTP/AT); 3D finite element model of blade + attachment
dataset_population_audit.testing_type: Numerical contact stress analysis (large-scale 3D FE with contact friction, orthotropy, primary/secondary crystal orientation); no new test data generated
dataset_population_audit.measured_quantities: None measured; calculated contact/attachment stresses vs. coefficient of friction and crystal orientation
observed_phenomena: Attachment stresses peak at locations where fretting cracks have been observed on SSME blades

relevance_to_fmea_gpt: Closes the blade attachment fretting gap (RET-13/RET-14): fretting fatigue at blade/disk attachment surfaces, role of friction coefficient, slip amplitude and contact pressure, crystallographic crack initiation in single-crystal blades.

dataset_population_audit.testing_type: Jet-fueled burner rig cyclic thermal exposure, static/cyclic furnace oxidation tests, mechanical property tests, life model correlation
